frequency_question: How often do federal agencies successfully complete the revocation of a recognized standard-setting or accrediting body's authority within a multi-year administrative window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal federal Department of Education or equivalent agency action attempting to withdraw recognition from an accrediting body under statutory administrative procedures. Excludes voluntary relinquishments or minor probationary sanctions that do not involve revocation of recognition.

cases.name: American Bar Association accreditation review (various past Department of Education review cycles)
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) first termination
ACICS reinstatement and subsequent final termination
American Bar Association periodic re-evaluation compliance proceedings

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 6 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.5x)
coverage_note: 6 major contested recognition battles identified since 1990; 2 resulted in actual formal revocation.
known_gaps: Excludes minor advisory committee warnings that did not reach formal Department head revocation orders.
skeleton: Total formal recognition withdrawal proceedings initiated against major national accrediting bodies by the U.S. Department of Education since 1990, divided into successful revocations versus settlements or renewals.
multiplier: 2 successful revocations out of roughly 6 major contested review/revocation proceedings initiated against established accrediting bodies since 1990.
validity_reason: Administrative procedures governing agency recognition and Higher Education Act statutory frameworks remain stable across multiple presidential administrations.
